title: Slide a repair coupling across a pipe joint
instruction: Join the new pipe to the installed pipe: lift the new pipe's loose end into line with the installed pipe, slide the coupling along the installed pipe until it is centred over the joint, then let go.
context: Plumbers and pipefitters (O*NET 47-2152.00 Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters) and building maintenance workers (49-9071.00) repair a damaged length of drain pipe by cutting it out, fitting a new length and closing the last joint with a slip coupling, a sleeve with no stop inside. The new length is already held at its other end, so the coupling cannot be pushed onto it end-first: one hand holds the new pipe in line while the other slides the coupling across the joint.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them; heights from the table top. A drain line of 1 1/2-inch PVC pipe (48.3 mm across) runs left to right 30 cm forward, its axis 10 cm above the table. On the right, a fixed installed pipe ends 2 cm right of the centre line; it rests in a steel clamp on a steel post 19 cm right of the centre line. On the left, a loose new pipe 25 cm long (190 g, its cut near end deburred) reaches from 2 mm left of the installed pipe's end to a fixed PVC elbow, its far end pushed home in the elbow's socket (3 cm deep, 1.2 mm of play all round); the elbow turns down to the table. The new pipe's near end rests on a fixed pine block (6 x 5 cm, 6.2 cm tall, 0.5 to 5.5 cm left of the centre line), so the pipe slopes 3.5 degrees and its near end sits about 1.5 cm below the installed pipe's end. A loose grey PVC slip coupling (70 mm long, bore 1.2 mm looser than the pipe all round, 5 mm walls, both mouths chamfered 30 degrees over 6 mm, 50 g) sits on the installed pipe, its middle 11 cm right of the centre line (9 cm from the joint). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler; partial credit is the best stage reached during the run, except that if the new pipe is pulled 2 cm or more out of the elbow, or a pipe or the coupling falls onto the table, the score is 0 for the rest of the run. 1.0: the coupling centred over the joint (each pipe at least 30 mm inside it), the new pipe in line (its near end's centre within 4 mm of the installed pipe's axis, sloping under 2 degrees) with its far end home in the elbow (within 5 mm), both grippers let go and at least 5 cm from the pipes and the coupling, everything still for 1 s. 0.75: the coupling centred and the new pipe in line and home, before the grippers have let go and moved clear, or before everything is still. 0.5: the coupling across the joint, each pipe at least 10 mm inside it, the new pipe in line. 0.25: the new pipe's near end lifted into line (within 4 mm of the installed pipe's axis). 0.0: anything else.
reset_notes: Slide the coupling back along the installed pipe until its middle is 9 cm from the joint, and lay the new pipe's near end back on the block with its far end home in the elbow; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the pipes, the elbow and the coupling are rigid PVC (dry friction 0.45); the coupling's bore and the elbow's socket are 16-sided (1.2 mm of play at the flats) instead of round, the deburred pipe end is a 1.5 mm step; no solvent cement, so the coupling holds the new pipe by its fit alone (a dry fit); the installed pipe and the elbow are fixed.
